notes: Dower action turning on who is 'tenant of the freehold' as between a vendor and vendee under articles of sale; no lodging/boarding issue. Retrieval matched on generic 'tenant of the freehold' phrase.
Debt action for rent on a family farm let by a now-deceased father to support the household; not a lodging or boarding-house case.
Covenant action for rent between co-tenants of a farm held under sealed articles resembling a partnership; no lodging issue.

holding_summary: A mail contractor's sub-agent boarded himself and stabled two teams of horses with Kimball at a stipulated weekly rate. The court held Kimball's claim arose as a livery-stable keeper rather than an innkeeper, since the arrangement differed from the entertainment of transient strangers and travellers, and upheld his joint and several lien on the horses for the keeping (including board).

quotes.text: The right of lien for the keeping of several horses of the same person at the same time is a charge; not against the horses, and therefore several and divided; but against the owner, secured by a lien upon all the horses, and therefore joint and several, and one horse may be detained for the keeping of all.

But it was not at all as innkeeper that the plaintiff became entitled to assert this claim against the defendant, but as livery-stable keeper; for it was under an arrangement totally different from that which tabes place in the entertainment of strangers and travellers.

It was a necessary part of that arrangement that the horses should be delivered to the defendant as they were needed, and this is part of the ordinary course of business of livery-stable keepers, and therefore must be consistent with the right of lien that belongs to the occupation.

notes: Core holding is about innkeeper/livery-stable lien law, but the court expressly distinguishes ordinary weekly-rate boarding-for-pay from the transient-guest innkeeper relation, bearing on characterization of compensated boarding arrangements. Marked mixed: enforces the boarding arrangement as ordinary business, but the case is not centrally about a householder letting a dwelling.

Partition action concerning a vendee's equitable estate and adverse possession; a lease of an absent heir's land share is mentioned only to show the defendant's possession was not adverse. No lodging issue.
Rent-apportionment dispute after a ferry-property landlord sold part of the reversion to a railroad; no lodging issue.

Trespass quare clausum fregit turning on whether a landlord of agricultural land had sufficient constructive possession to sue before entry, given a tenant-at-will occupant (son-in-law). Tenancy-at-will doctrine, not lodging.
Assumpsit for use and occupation against a tenant who paid rent to a decedent's administrator rather than the true heirs; estate-administration/landlord-tenant dispute, not lodging.
Distress-for-rent case on a leased, stocked dairy farm; addresses whether 'rent' can issue from land plus furniture/chattels. No lodging issue.
Trover action over ownership of steam saw-mill machinery/fixtures after a milling agreement expired; fixtures law, no lodging issue.
Landlord-tenant summary proceeding over an agricultural 'improving lease' (clear/fence land, pay taxes in lieu of rent); addresses timing of notice to quit, not lodging.

Dispute over an alien's right to vote in a Pittsburgh borough election as a 'freeholder, housekeeper, or inhabitant.' 'Housekeeper' functions as a voter-qualification term here, unconnected to letting rooms or dwellings.

Landlord-tenant-act jurisdiction case holding a roughly seven-month lease of a house (rent = taxes plus repairs) qualifies as a 'term of one or more years' for summary-possession purposes. Confirms short leases of a dwelling are treated as ordinary tenancies for years, but the case is purely procedural statutory construction, not about lodging/boarding characterization, and no household-letting facts are at issue; kept irrelevant per the no-quote/passing-mention standard.
Landlord-tenant summary proceeding quashed for defects in the inquisition record concerning a rent-free tenancy at will; no lodging issue.
Landlord-tenant summary proceeding quashed for defective inquisition findings on a one-year farm lease; no lodging issue.

Slave-freedom (homine replegiando) case turning on whether an enslaved person's 'sojourning' in Pennsylvania with a farm-lessee's family, without the master's consent, triggered the abolition statute. 'Sojourning' here concerns residency of an enslaved person, unrelated to lodger/boarder letting of dwellings.
Landlord-tenant summary proceeding on a one-year farm lease, addressing whether notice to quit must precede expiration of the term. No lodging issue.

Replevin over a distress for rent on a one-year lease of a tavern property; the tenant's covenant to 'keep a public house' and obtain the license is recited only as a lease term and is never adjudicated. The actual holding concerns whether rent payable in advance was a properly reserved, distrainable rent, not innkeeping/lodging characterization.
